card.summary: 10 GB free; VIP 3 TB and SVIP 6 TB. A new account that saves one shared file gets 1 TB: '新用户保存一次别人分享的文件，可获取1TB的空间容量'

free_tier.stated: 10 GB free; VIP 3 TB and SVIP 6 TB. A new account that saves one shared file gets 1 TB: '新用户保存一次别人分享的文件，可获取1TB的空间容量'

per_object_cap.stated: Not published for the free tier. Downloads above 50 MB need a desktop-client user agent and a cookie, else the API answers 23018 download file size limit

retention.stated: Accounts frozen after 12 months without a login, with the storage reclaimed if not unfrozen within a month: '超过1年未登录 … 回收存储容量 … 文件丢失、数据清空'

egress.terms: No per-GB fee, but the free tier is shaped to 2 to 4 MB/s against about 50 MB/s on SVIP, and a third-party fetch service measured a free account at about 60 KB/s. Downloads above 50 MB need a client user agent and a cookie

record.tooling: no official open API. The reverse-engineered web API at drive-pc.quark.cn is what the OpenList quark driver uses; the netdisk-fast-download qk parser states that a logged-in cookie is mandatory; the OpenList docs warn quick-transfer now needs a local agent because of the speed limit
record.chaining: Base free storage is 10 GB per mobile-verified account. Promotional 1 TB allocations granted upon saving shared files expire after promotional periods rather than providing permanent capacity.

limits.value: 2 to 4 MB/s on the free tier
12 months without a login freezes the account and reclaims the capacity
share downloads above 50 MB need a desktop-client user agent and a cookie

identity_cost.detail: mainland +86 only, and SVIP payment needs a Chinese identity document

record.reliability_note: The anonymous path gets metadata and not bytes: a share token and a full file listing with fid and share_fid_token come back with no cookie at all, and the download call is 404 on all four documented hosts. Download tickets are IP-bound, so a link minted on one host dies when replayed from another, which is why every public Quark parser rots within weeks

evidence.proved: 'SVIP用户6TB空间，VIP用户3TB空间，普通用户初始容量10GB空间'
'超过1年未登录 … 回收存储容量 … 文件丢失、数据清空'
200, 756 B, data.stoken returned with a share title and no cookie
200, 3,016 B, list[0] with a file name, size 31614114, fid and share_fid_token, no cookie
404 on pan.quark.cn, drive-pc.quark.cn, drive-h.quark.cn and drive.quark.cn, all four
'分享通道绕过 无效, PC API 上 share/sharepage/download 等均 404'; downloads above 50 MB need a client UA and a cookie

record.binding_note: 10 GB free, and 2 to 4 MB/s is 170 to 340 GB a day at best, so the quota and the shaping both fail. The shaping is the one that would still bind on a paid tier, and the identity gate sits in front of both.
record.notes: Quark has largely replaced Baidu Pan as the default share host on Chinese forums, which is why it is recorded in full. The finding that matters for a bridge builder is that the anonymous token lists a whole share and cannot move a byte, and that download tickets are IP-bound so a harvested cookie does not survive a replay.

record.provider: Quark TV and UC TV (夸克网盘 TV版, UC网盘 TV版)
record.category: TV-edition OAuth client for a Chinese pan

free_tier.stated: Quark free 300 GB plus one-off 1 TB gift campaigns; two documented campaigns give 2 TB total. UC's free base is 10 GB

per_object_cap.stated: Not published for the TV client

retention.stated: The gift campaigns are one-off per account and campaign-gated. No retention clock on stored files

egress.terms: Quark free is shaped to about 1.7 MB/s and about 5 MB/s at peak for 88VIP. The TV client streams in original quality without downloading, which is why the community uses it

record.tooling: a reverse-engineered TV OAuth client, fully documented in source: the OpenList quark_uc_tv driver hard-codes api https://open-api-drive.quark.cn for Quark and https://open-api-drive.uc.cn for UC, with a public client id, a TV sign key, an app version and a channel. WebDAV comes out once mounted
record.chaining: The TV OAuth reads an account through a clean API with no client, so it is a serving and STRM path and not a write path. Paired with a writable pan it covers both directions, which is why the community keeps it alive

limits.value: the TV client is read-only by design: the driver sets NoUpload and NoOverwriteUpload
free egress shaped to about 1.7 MB/s

identity_cost.detail: a Quark or UC account, which is phone-bound in practice; the TV client's own login path exists but does not remove the account requirement

record.reliability_note: The TV client's client id and sign key are public constants that Alibaba rotates, and when they rotate every mount breaks until the driver is re-patched. The free-tier space campaigns are monthly and quantity-capped, so they are a lottery and not a capacity plan

evidence.proved: two drivers, QuarkTV and UCTV, both API endpoints, the client id, signKey, app version, channel, and NoUpload: true with NoOverwriteUpload: true
HTTP 400, 65 B, {"status":-1,"errno":10001,"error_info":"_timestamp格式错误"}, so the endpoint is live and wants a signed timestamp
two campaigns of 1 TB each, so 2 TB permanent

evidence.proved: the endpoint is live and answers a body of 65 bytes that wants a signed timestamp

record.binding_note: 300 GB free, and the TV client cannot write at all, so the direction that fails is the write side: it is a download-and-stream path with no upload, which makes it a serving helper and not a store.
record.notes: The canonical inverse of the public-instance problem. There an instance advertises a write it refuses; here a client is documented as read-only by design. Both are cases where the API's write surface must be read from the driver's own flags and not from the marketing page.
